full_judgment: 14. I have my anxious thoughts to this question and have been unable to persuade myself as to why such changes or reversal in the interpretation of law or in the application of law to facts will render the bar of res judicata ineffective. The few occasions when the bar of res judicata are removed are inter alia when the law governing the earlier decision has been altered by a competent authority, when the decision relates to the jurisdiction of the Court to try the earlier proceeding and when the earlier decision declares valid a transaction which is prohibited by law. Barring these situations previous decision on an issue of law or a mixed issue of fact and law will be res judicata in a subsequent proceeding between the same parties, the reason being that the previous decision on a matter in issue alone is res judicata. The reasons for the decision are not res judicata.
